# Verification and reproducibility {#sec-ch16}

The chapters before this one each end with a Tests layer: the ctest entries that check that chapter's claims,
with the tolerance each one uses. This chapter is about the checks that sit above any single chapter. Some of
them change no line of `src/`; they are rules for deciding whether two builds compute the same thing, whether a
shipped test still passes when the stage executor captures it, how many launches a step costs, and which test
holds which past defect. The tools behind the first and third of these are committed on the closing-plan branch,
not in the snapy tree at the pin; the chapter names them by path and cites that branch in its footnotes.

@sec-ch16-gates describes the two bitwise gates, which compare the state of two builds byte for byte on a fixed
set of decks. @sec-ch16-capture describes the capture sweep: every shipped test run under the default execution
on CUDA[^rg-5a7220aa0c8b], sorted into captured, refused and failed. @sec-ch16-launches gives the launch-counting procedure that
@sec-ch11 cites for its cost table. @sec-ch16-regressions lists the regression tests with the defect each one
pins. @sec-ch16-devices says what is compared across CPU[^rg-8c5110e2586a], CUDA and MPS[^rg-5a8fdd30db1b], and to what tolerance.

The sections from @sec-ch16-metrics on are the verification catalogue: how to read the evidence of a test
(@sec-ch16-metrics), the invariant checks (@sec-ch16-invariants), and one evidence section per chapter it covers.
Their PROVENANCE blocks name the commit each was read at; each per-chapter section moves into the Tests layer of
the chapter it covers when that chapter is written at the code pin, and the chapters cite them until then.

The multi-rank test selections run serially (`ctest -j 1`). Several registrations start `torchrun` without
`--standalone`, so they meet at its default rendezvous port 29500, and `ctest -j` does not assign ports;
concurrent launches need a distinct `--master-port` each ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}).

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bitwise gates (@sec-ch16-gates) | none (a tool run on two builds) | not run by ctest | exact (byte for byte), same device | none at the pin |
| Capture sweep (@sec-ch16-capture) | `integration/execution` | `auto` (cuda-graph on CUDA) | exact against eager | `test_stage_executor_capture_python` |
| Launch counting (@sec-ch16-launches) | `bench.py --profile` | not run by ctest | a count, no tolerance | none at the pin |
| Regression provenance (@sec-ch16-regressions) | none (a record) | not applicable | per test (@tbl-ch16-regressions) | the tests listed there |
| Device reproducibility (@sec-ch16-devices) | the device | CPU | exact within a device; $10^{-12}$ CUDA against CPU per line; $\max(10^{-4}, 3\,e_{64})$ MPS against CPU | `test_mps_matches_cpu_python` |

: The sections of this chapter, the switch each one turns on, its default, the precision it asks for, and the
test that carries it. The tolerances are stated in each section's Tests layer. {#tbl-ch16-schemes}
